result.rationale: The diff shows addGuests.handler.ts performing `prisma.booking.update` with `attendees: { createMany: ... }` before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. If calendar sync throws, there is no rollback or error handling around it, so the DB retains the new guests. On retry, `uniqueGuests` filters out any guest already in `booking.attendees`, and since none remain, the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid`, blocking recovery. This non-atomic commit-then-sync ordering is fully visible in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, the code first updates the database with new attendees (prisma.booking.update around line 85-100), then later calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) to sync with the calendar. If the calendar sync fails, the database already has the new attendees committed. On retry, the uniqueGuests filter (lines 68-72) will filter out these guests since they're already in booking.attendees, resulting in an empty list and throwing 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error. This is a real atomicity bug where partial failure leaves inconsistent state.
